pass_a_gloss: [...] as we are, and entered the measure of the emptying. And he speaks to the chosen, and says that, In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you. Christ had been foreknown before foundation of world, and his mystery; but he shone forth at times which the Sovereign wished, at which he has helped us; and the time of the becoming man he says is a day of salvation. For thus somewhere also the divine Paul: Behold now, he says, a well-acceptable time, behold now a day of salvation. And the prophet David sings too and says: This is the day which the Lord made, let us exult and be glad in it. [Lemma, Isaiah 49:8-12:] And I gave you for a covenant of nations, to establish the earth, and to inherit an inheritance of desert, saying to those in bonds: Come out; and to those in the darkness: Be uncovered. And in all their ways they will be fed, and in all the paths their pasture. They will not hunger, nor thirst, nor will burning heat strike them, nor the sun; but the one pitying them will comfort, and will lead them through springs of waters. And I will set every mountain for a road, and every path for pasture to them. Behold these come from far. These from north, and these from sea, and others from land of Persians. It seemed good to some of the interpreters who came before to make the beginning of the present chapter: Thus says the Lord: In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you. And they say these things were said by God and Father to the Saviour of us all, Christ. And they weave in besides also some such sense. For he prayed, he says, before the precious cross, saying: Father, if possible, let this cup pass from me; and he was not heard, for he drank it. And since he trampled death, the Father helping, the 'In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you' was said to him necessarily. But the account seems to me to be very weak in plausibility. For although knowing that he must drink the cup, and that the [world] under heaven would not come to be able to be saved except through the death of his flesh and the resurrection from dead, most providentially the form of the prayer was done, so that the begging off from the passion might accuse the bloodshed of the Jews; since in what manner would Israel have become liable to the charges of impiety toward him, unless the suffering was unwilled by him because of the shame? But even so it became willed, both to remove from the world the sin and to reshape our things into newness of holy life. For thus you will understand also the thing said by him, that: I have come down from the heaven, not so that I may do my own will, but the wi[ll] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … like us, and entered the measure of self-emptying. He addresses the chosen and says: “In an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you” (Isaiah 49:8). Christ and His mystery were foreknown before the foundation of the world (1 Peter 1:20), but they shone forth at the times the Sovereign willed, the times at which He has helped us; and the time of the incarnation he calls a day of salvation. So too, somewhere, the divine Paul says: “Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation” (2 Corinthians 6:2). And the prophet David sings and says: “This is the day that the Lord has made; let us exult and be glad in it” (Psalm 118:24).

“And I have given you as a covenant to the nations, to establish the earth and to inherit the inheritance of the desert, saying to those in bonds, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ And in all their ways they will be fed, and in all the paths will be their pasture. They will not hunger or thirst, nor will the burning heat or the sun strike them; but He who has mercy on them will comfort them, and will lead them by springs of water. And I will make every mountain a road, and every path a pasture for them. Behold, these come from afar, these from the north, and these from the sea, and others from the land of the Persians” (Isaiah 49:8–12).

Some of the earlier interpreters decided to make the beginning of the present chapter the words: “Thus says the Lord: In an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you” (Isaiah 49:8). And they say that these words were spoken by God the Father to Christ, the Savior of us all. They weave in besides a meaning of this kind. He prayed, they say, before the precious cross, saying: “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me” (Matthew 26:39); and He was not heard, for He drank it. But since He trampled on death with the Father’s help, the words “In an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you” were of necessity said to Him.

But this account seems to me to be sorely lacking in plausibility. For He knew that He had to drink the cup, and that the world under heaven could not come to be saved except through the death of His flesh and the resurrection from the dead. Even so, He went through the form of the prayer as a carefully chosen step in the divine plan, so that His begging to be spared the Passion might accuse the bloodguilt of the Jews. For how would Israel have become liable to the charges of impiety against Him, if suffering had not been against His will because of its shame? Yet even so it became His will, both to take away sin from the world and to remake our state into the newness of a holy life (compare Romans 6:4). For in this way one will understand also His saying: “I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will …” (John 6:38).

τὸ τῆς
κενώ- σεως ὑπέδυ μέτρον
choices.why: The Son entered the measure of self-emptying; it was not poured out upon us.
rejected: the measure of emptiness has been poured out upon us

choices.english: I have given you as a covenant to the nations
choices.why: Isaiah 49:8: God gives the Servant as a covenant; the Lord does not give a covenant to the nations.
rejected: The Lord gave a covenant to the nations

choices.why: The cup of Gethsemane was not taken away; he drank it.
